title: PetAssetDescriptor
description: Shape of the descriptor a pet animation asset must satisfy, for pet/contracts/rive-state-machine@2.0.0. It is the boundary between a designed .riv file and the runtime that drives it: the artboard the runtime loads, the state machine it runs, and the inputs it writes. Version 2.0.0 declares two independent layers where 1.0.0 declared one input. The second layer is not new behaviour — req-018-pet-liveness specified and measured it — but it was absent from the declared interface, so an asset authored outside the product could not satisfy the specification it was required to satisfy. What this file cannot express is stated by the contract document and is a property of the binary asset rather than of the descriptor: whether the named artboard, state machine and layer inputs are actually present in the file, and whether a declared capability resolves to transitions the asset can play. An asset whose descriptor is satisfied and whose artboard is missing is refused at load and the shipped default pack is presented instead.

artboardName.description: The root artboard carrying the character meshes, skeletons and animation hierarchy. Renaming it is a MAJOR change, because every asset already produced would stop loading.

stateMachineName.description: The single state machine the canvas runtime loads and executes. The runtime plays no animation by name; driving one directly is forbidden, because it would bypass the blend curves the asset declares.

inputs.description: The inputs the runtime writes, one per animation layer. The work status layer is required because it is what makes the pet report the system's state, and a pet that cannot do that is not this product's pet. The locomotion layer is optional at the descriptor level: a pack that omits it is valid and borrows the shipped default pack's locomotion for that capability alone, which is the per-capability substitution the model records as INV-PACK-02. An asset may declare further optional triggers of its own, which the runtime never writes.

workStatus.description: The layer reporting what the system is doing. It carries the same five values and the same numbering as the single input of 1.0.0, so an asset's authored transitions survive the revision unchanged; what changed is the input's name and the fact that it is now one layer of two.

default.description: The state the pet holds before the application has said anything. It is 0, the idle state, so an asset that fails to receive a first value still renders a resting character rather than a blank canvas.

locomotion.description: The layer reporting how the pet is moving. Independent of the work status layer: a status change during movement must not interrupt the movement, which is the orthogonality req-018-pet-liveness measured at 60 fps with no stutter.

default.description: The locomotion state the pet holds before the application has said anything. It is 0, standing, so a pack whose first value never arrives renders a character at rest rather than mid-stride.

transitionBlendDurationMs.description: The blend duration configured in the asset between two states of either layer. The measured latency from writing an input to the first blended frame was 2.9 ms to 15.1 ms on Windows and 1.3 ms to 15.8 ms on macOS, well inside this window — VERIFIED (spikes/SP-3-electron-rive/REPORT.md#0-ket-luan, spikes/SP-3-electron-rive/macos/REPORT.md#0-ket-luan). A duration outside the window is refused at load because the character reads either as snapping or as unresponsive.
